# International Migration Review Forum 2026

> The second International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) will take place at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 5-8 May 2026 and will be preceded by an informal multistakeholder hearing on 4 May 2026.

## About the Forum

In 2018, Member States agreed to review progress at the local, national, regional, and global levels in implementing the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) within the United Nations framework, through a State-led approach and with the participation of all relevant stakeholders. 

The second quadrennial International Migration Review Forum will be hosted by the President of the UN General Assembly (PGA) in New York from 5-8 May to review progress on GCM Implementation and set the direction for the next five years. 

It consists of four interactive multi-stakeholder round tables, a policy debate, and a plenary, preceded by an informal interactive multi-stakeholder hearing, hosted by PGA on 4 May. It will result in an inter-governmentally agreed Progress Declaration.

## Programme

Informal interactive multi-stakeholder hearing 

The Informal Interactive Multi-Stakeholder Hearing provides an inclusive and participatory platform forstakeholders, in to engage directly with Member States ahead of the IMRF. The hearing enables diverse perspectives, lived experiences, and evidence-based recommendations to inform deliberations and contribute to the development of the Progress Declaration. 

 

 Multi-stakeholder Hearing - IMRF 2026 Draft Agenda 

01 May 2026

Round tables

The four round tables will offer space for discussion covering all 23 objectives of the Global Compact with the aim of reviewing the progress made in its implementation at all levels, bearing in mind that the Global Compact is based on a set of cross-cutting and interdependent guiding principles. 

 Round Tables 1 Webcast and statements (5 May) 

Policy Debate 

The Director General of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), as Coordinator of the Network, will facilitate the policy debate focusing on challenges in the implementation of the Global Compact, including the links with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the capacity-building mechanism and contemporary and emerging issues related to migration. 

The policy debate will also consider possible guidance for the United Nations system to strengthen its efforts in improving system-wide effectiveness and coherence and in supporting Member States in implementing the Global Compact, upon the request of Member States, based on their national policies and priorities. 

The Side Events will provide an opportunity to discuss good practices, challenges and recommendations to further the implementation of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. 

The Side Events calendars will be updated on a rolling basis. Confirmed side events will be reflected in the calendars, including registration links for events (as applicable).

#### Progress Declaration and Co-Facilitators Updates

Co-facilitators

For the IMRF 2026, the President of the General Assembly appointed H.E. Mr. Erastus Lokaale, Permanent Representative of Kenya, and H.E. Mr. Olivier Maes, Permanent Representative of Luxembourg, as co-facilitators to lead the process toward the Progress Declaration. In this role, they are mandated to conduct open, transparent and inclusive intergovernmental consultations with Member States and stakeholders, guide negotiations, and steer the drafting of the 2026 Progress Declaration to be adopted at the IMRF.

Indicative Progress declaration Roadmap

Progress Declaration

The Progress Declaration is the inter-governmentally negotiated outcome document of the IMRF. It reflects Member States’ collective assessment of progress in implementing the GCM, identifies remaining gaps and challenges, and outlines priorities and commitments to accelerate implementation in the years ahead.

## Voluntary GCM Progress Reports

Member States are invited to submit voluntary GCM Reports to share progress on implementing the Compact. The reports are prepared through inclusive, multi-stakeholder consultations and provide evidence to inform the 2026 IMRF. Explore submitted reports, access reporting guidance, and learn about the support available to Member States. 

## Make a Pledge

The GCM Pledging Initiative has been relaunched ahead of the IMRF 2026 and invites pledges from Member States, UN entities, stakeholders, and the private sector.

A pledge is a concrete and measurable commitment made by UN Member and Observer States, UN entities and relevant stakeholders - from financial institution to private sector entities and to civil society and diaspora organizations - to advance the GCM implementation.

Learn more & make a pledge: The Pledging Dashboard. For more information or support, contact the UN Network Secretariat at pledges@iom.int 

Share your country’s experiences and learn from others in implementing the Global Compact on Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration. The Repository of Practices collects examples from governments and stakeholders worldwide – submit your practice to contribute to global learning and collaboration.
